variants.specifics: Pip, Brother Anselm's novice, went into the old barrow east of the ford after the Urchins who stole the chapel's candlesticks; Anselm begs the player to find him.

plea.speaker: Anselm
plea.text:
Please, wait. My novice, Pip, a boy of twelve, went into the old barrow east of the ford yesterday, after the Urchins that stole our altar candlesticks. He said they were the chapel's and he'd have them back. He hasn't come home.

I'm no fighter, and the town has no one to spare. Find him. Bring him home to me.

reminder.speaker: Anselm
reminder.text: Any word of Pip? The barrow's east of the ford, past the willows. Please hurry; it's cold under the ground.

found.speaker: Pip
found.text: You're not an Urchin! Oh, thank the Ford. They chased me down into the deep room and I hid behind the bones. I didn't get the candlesticks. Brother Anselm will be so cross. Will you take me home?

following.speaker: Pip
following.text: I'm right behind you. I'll stay close. Closer than that, even.

completion.speaker: Anselm
completion.text: Pip! You young fool, come here. ...Thank you. The candlesticks can stay with the Urchins for all I care. Take these from the chapel's stores, and the ankh from our altar. It has kept better folk than me alive.

journal.text: Brother Anselm's novice Pip went into the old barrow east of the ford after the Urchins who stole the chapel's candlesticks, and has not come back. Anselm begs me to find him and bring him home to the Chapel of the Ford.

variants.specifics: Wenna's son Robin, ten, chased a strayed lamb into the Ashwood and is treed by wolves; Wenna begs.

plea.speaker: Wenna
plea.text: Robin's not come home. My boy. He went after a lamb that strayed into the Ashwood this morning, and the shepherds say the wolves are down from the deep wood. Please. He's ten. He'll have climbed something; he always climbs. Find him.

reminder.speaker: Wenna
reminder.text: Have you found him? Into the Ashwood, past Ulric's folds. Listen for him; he never stops talking.

found.speaker: Robin
found.text: Up here! Are they gone? I've been up this tree since the sun was over there. The lamb ran off. Is my mum angry? Can I come down now?

following.speaker: Robin
following.text: Are there any more wolves? You go first. I'll hold on to your belt. Not really. Nearly.

completion.speaker: Wenna
completion.text: Robin! Where have you been, you... come here. Oh, come here. Thank you, traveller. It's only what was in the jar, and potions for the road; I'd give you the mill if I could.

journal.text: Robin, the ten-year-old son of Wenna the miller's widow, went into the Ashwood after a strayed lamb and has not come home. The wolves are down from the deep wood. Wenna begs me to find him.

variants.specifics: Edwy the ferryman, taken by Corwin's bandits to row their loot across the Bracken at night, is tied up in the watchtower; his wife Bess begs.

plea.speaker: Bess
plea.text: They took my Edwy. Corwin's men, on the north road, three days ago; they wanted a ferryman to take their loot across the Bracken by night. He's in that tower on Crow Hill. The reeve says he can't spare a man. I'm asking you. Bring him home.

reminder.speaker: Bess
reminder.text: Is he...? The tower's on Crow Hill, north of town. Please.

found.speaker: Edwy
found.text: Who's that? Not one of them. Bess sent you, didn't she. She would. Get these ropes off me; I've rowed my last for Red Corwin.

following.speaker: Edwy
following.text: My legs are stiff as oars. Go on, I'm with you. Don't stop for me.

completion.speaker: Bess
completion.text: Edwy! Oh, you're thin; what did they feed you? ...Here, traveller, take it, take it all. It's what we'd put by for the new boat. We'll build it next year.

journal.text: Red Corwin's bandits took Edwy the ferryman off the north road to row their loot across the Bracken at night. His wife Bess begs me to bring him home from the watchtower on Crow Hill.

variants.specifics: Mabry's apprentice Linnet went down into the flooded crypt under the Chapel of the Ford for grave-moss and is trapped among spiders; Mabry begs.

plea.speaker: Mabry
plea.text: My apprentice, Linnet. I sent her down into the crypt under the Chapel of the Ford for grave-moss, it only grows there, and she hasn't come up. Brother Anselm says the river's in the crypt again, and there are spiders down there the size of my hand. Bigger. I sent her. Please go and look.

reminder.speaker: Mabry
reminder.text: The crypt stair is behind the chapel altar. Anselm will let you down. Please hurry.

found.speaker: Linnet
found.text: Is that a light? Oh, please, I'm here! On the tomb; the water's all round it. The spiders are in the walls. I got the moss, though. Mabry will want the moss.

following.speaker: Linnet
following.text: Mind the third step, it's gone. And the webs. I'm right behind you. I won't drop the moss.

completion.speaker: Mabry
completion.text: Linnet! You're soaked through... and you got the moss, you mad girl. Thank you. Take these, and the book; she's copied every receipt in it and doesn't need it now. Do you, love?

journal.text: Mabry's apprentice Linnet went down into the crypt under the Chapel of the Ford for grave-moss and has not come up. The river is in the crypt again, and spiders with it. Mabry begs me to find her.

variants.specifics: Ossian's daughter Merry went into the Reedmere downstream looking for the lantern the inn is named for, and is lost among the marsh lights; Ossian begs.

plea.speaker: Ossian
plea.text: My girl, Merry. She's got it into her head she'll find the lantern the inn's named for, the one the river took off the ford post, out in the Reedmere downstream. She went at dusk. There are lights out there at night that aren't lanterns. Please. Find her before they do.

reminder.speaker: Ossian
reminder.text: The Reedmere's down the river, south of the ford. Keep to the hummocks; the mud will have your boots.

found.speaker: Merry
found.text: I followed the lights. I thought one was the lantern. It wasn't. It laughed. Can we go home? I'm cold, and I've lost a shoe.

following.speaker: Merry
following.text: I'll step where you step. Don't look at the lights. Da says don't look at the lights.

completion.speaker: Ossian
completion.text: Merry! Sit by the fire, you're blue. ...Traveller, your room's free as long as you're in Brackenford, and take this. It's the inn's takings for the week. Not much, with the road shut.

journal.text: Ossian's daughter Merry went out into the Reedmere, downstream of the ford, looking for the lantern the Drowned Lantern is named for, and has not come back. There are lights in the marsh at night. Ossian begs me to find her.

variants.specifics: Brother Anselm himself went to the old barrow to ask the Urchins for the candlesticks and was thrown in a pit; Pip begs.

plea.speaker: Pip
plea.text: Please, you have to help. Brother Anselm went down to the old barrow to talk to the Urchins, to ask for the candlesticks back nicely, he said. He took bread for them. That was this morning. He's old, and his knees are bad, and he hasn't come back.

reminder.speaker: Pip
reminder.text: The barrow's east of the ford. Please hurry. I've lit every candle we have left.

found.speaker: Anselm
found.text: Ah. I'd hoped my next visitor would be friendlier. No, I'm unhurt; they took the bread and my sandals and put me in this pit to think about it. Pip sent you? Bless him. Let's go, before they finish thinking.

following.speaker: Anselm
following.text: Slowly, if you'll forgive an old man. My knees were not made for barrows.

completion.speaker: Pip
completion.text: Brother! You've no shoes! ...Thank you. Brother Anselm says I'm to give you the ankh from the altar, and the chapel's coin box. There's not much in it. I'd give you more if we had it.

journal.text: Brother Anselm went down to the old barrow east of the ford to ask the Urchins for the chapel's candlesticks, and has not come back. His novice Pip begs me to find him.

variants.specifics: Dunstan's apprentice Corin went to dig ore in the old drift mine under Crow Hill, walled up for a reason, and has not come out; Dunstan begs.

plea.speaker: Dunstan
plea.text: My apprentice, Corin. With no iron coming down the north road, the fool went to the old drift mine under Crow Hill to dig ore himself. Two days gone. The miners walled that drift up in my father's time, for a reason nobody would tell me. Bring the lad back and I'll owe you.

reminder.speaker: Dunstan
reminder.text: The drift's in the face of Crow Hill, below the tower. Mind the bandits. Mind the dark more.

found.speaker: Corin
found.text: Master Dunstan sent you? He'll kill me. Better him than what's down the far end. Something walks there and drags its feet. I've a sack of ore. Can I bring it?

following.speaker: Corin
following.text: I've got the sack. I'm keeping up. Don't go back that way, whatever you hear.

completion.speaker: Dunstan
completion.text: Corin, you thick-headed... is that ore? ...Traveller, thank you. Take this, and these draughts from Mabry's. I bought them for him, and he doesn't deserve them.

journal.text: Dunstan the smith's apprentice Corin went to dig ore in the old drift mine under Crow Hill, which the miners walled up long ago, and has not come back. Dunstan begs me to bring him home.

variants.specifics: Reeve Halvard's son Ewan rode out alone after Corwin's bandits, was thrown from his horse and lies hurt in a ditch on the north road; Halvard begs as a father.

plea.speaker: Halvard
plea.text: This isn't the reeve asking. This is a father. My son, Ewan, rode out of the north gate last night before I could stop him, to prove to the town he's worth something. His horse came home this morning without him. Corwin's men ride that road. Find him. Alive, if he is.

reminder.speaker: Halvard
reminder.text: Anything? The north road, toward Crow Hill. Garrick will let you through the gate. Go.

found.speaker: Ewan
found.text: Don't... oh. You're not one of them. My leg's done; the horse threw me into this ditch and I've lain here all night listening to them ride past. Did my father send you? He'll never let me forget this.

following.speaker: Ewan
following.text: I can walk, if it's slow. Don't tell him I cried.

completion.speaker: Halvard
completion.text: Ewan. ...Sit. Someone fetch Brother Anselm to that leg. Traveller, what I have: the Moot Hall's purse, and an ankh Anselm gave me when the boy was born. Better it goes with you.

journal.text: Reeve Halvard's son Ewan rode out alone after Corwin's bandits on the north road, and his horse came home without him. Halvard begs me to find him.

variants.specifics: Old Maud, the half-blind bell-ringer of the chapel, went mushrooming in the Ashwood and is lost among the wolves; her grandson Davy begs.

plea.speaker: Davy
plea.text: It's my gran, Maud. She went mushrooming in the Ashwood, like every autumn, and she can't see past her own hand, and she's not back, and the wolves... I can't go; she made me promise I'd never go in there. You could. Please.

reminder.speaker: Davy
reminder.text: She'll be where the mushrooms are, under the big beeches. She sings when she's lost. Listen for singing.

found.speaker: Maud
found.text: Who's that? You've a kind step, whoever you are. Davy sent you, did he, the worrier. I'm not lost; I know exactly which tree I'm under. I just don't know where the tree is. Lend me your arm.

following.speaker: Maud
following.text: Not so fast; I've a basket. Mind the mushrooms. Mind the wolves too, I suppose.

completion.speaker: Davy
completion.text: Gran! ...Thank you. She says to give you her red draughts; she brews them herself. They taste of feet, but they work. And the purse. And a kiss, she says, but I'll not.

journal.text: Maud, the half-blind old woman who rings the chapel bell, went mushrooming in the Ashwood and has not come home. Her grandson Davy begs me to find her before the wolves do.

variants.specifics: Gytha, Garrick's wife, crossed to the haunted old toll-house on the far bank of the Bracken for firewood and her punt drifted home without her; Garrick, who cannot leave the gate, begs.

plea.speaker: Garrick
plea.text:
I can't leave the gate, the reeve's orders, and it's killing me. My wife, Gytha, poled the punt across to the old toll-house on the far bank to fetch our winter wood. That was noon. The punt's come back down the river empty.

Nobody goes in that toll-house after dark. Something lives in it that used to be the toll-keeper.

reminder.speaker: Garrick
reminder.text: The far bank, downstream: the ruin with no roof. There's a skiff at the ferry stage. Please.

found.speaker: Gytha
found.text: Garrick sent you? Thank the Ford. The punt slipped its rope and I couldn't swim for it, and when the sun went down the old keeper came out of the walls asking for his penny. I've been hiding in the chimney. Get me out of here.

following.speaker: Gytha
following.text: Row; I'll bail. Don't look back at the windows. He's still asking for his penny.

completion.speaker: Garrick
completion.text: Gytha! ...You're shaking. Here, my cloak. Traveller, you've a friend at the north gate for life. Take this; it's a month's pay, and the potions the reeve gives the watch.

journal.text: Gytha, the wife of Garrick the gate guard, crossed the Bracken to the old toll-house on the far bank for firewood, and her punt came back without her. Garrick cannot leave the gate and begs me to bring her home.
